I'm not sure the whole philosophy of long-term incarceration isn't fundamentally flawed. The word penitentiary comes from the word penitent. It's built on moral an religious reasoning, not logical reasoning. It was this idea that isolating people from the outside world would cause them to become closer to God.

Jail used to be a place you waited until society figured out how to deal with you. I wonder if a system of corporal punishment, public shaming, balanced with the best possible treatment for actual rehabilitation.. Fuck, phone's struggling.. I wonder if it's not the worst idea. I don't think a life-sentence is any less cruel than a death-sentence, if we decide someone really cannot be allowed to return to society.

There are violent crimes, and crimes of greed whose root causes could be prevented with psychological treatment, LSD Therapy, whatever works. There are crimes of desperation, if you can address the reasons why that person was desperate to begin with then that problem's solved.
